title: Working zones in a dental surgery: where contamination can and cannot go
audience: Cleaners and service workers who clean or restock dental surgeries and clinics.
learningOutcomes: Describe where contamination travels in a dental operatory and why the room is divided into zones.
Apply the rule for movement between the two zones.
Choose the correct glove and the correct storage point at changeover.

instruction.heading: Why the operatory is zoned
instruction.body: A dental treatment room has two kinds of working space. The first is the contaminated side, where patient fluids such as blood and saliva can land through splashing, spattering or transfer. It takes in the operating field and the area where instruments are cleaned. The second is the clean side, which holds reception, offices, staff rooms, sterile items and stock. The division keeps contamination inside the first side and stops it reaching the second. Everyone who works in the room has to understand where that line sits, not only the clinician.

instruction.heading: How far contamination travels
instruction.body: Splashes and large droplets usually land within roughly a metre of the patient's mouth. Finer aerosols produced during treatment can carry further than that. The source therefore treats the whole operatory as at risk while treatment is under way. Any surface or item within reach of the treatment is taken to be contaminated by that treatment. Surfaces left uncovered by a barrier are wiped down once each patient has left. An item placed on the contaminated side and not used is still treated as contaminated.

instruction.heading: Moving between the two sides
instruction.body: Staff may step from the clean side onto the contaminated side once they have gloved, but gloved hands carrying contaminated material do not travel back. Stock moves from clean storage into the room. Contaminated items never return to clean storage. Bulk stock such as glove boxes, cotton rolls and gauze stays on the clean side, covered against splashes and aerosols. Personal bags, spare clothing and personal belongings stay out of both sides.

instruction.heading: Your part at changeover
instruction.body: A cleaner who enters the room at changeover puts on fresh gloves before touching any working surface. Gloves that were on during assistance with the last procedure are not reused for the cleaning task. Working surfaces are wiped with neutral detergent by the method the practice's written protocol sets. Barrier coverings on hard-to-clean equipment are removed and replaced as the protocol requires. Never move a contaminated item into clean storage, and never open a clean drawer while wearing contaminated gloves.

procedure: Identify which side of the dividing line is clean before you enter the room.
Put on fresh gloves before wiping any working surface at changeover.
Use neutral detergent and the method the practice protocol sets for each surface.
Leave bulk stock outside the contaminated side, and keep it covered.
Keep personal bags and spare clothing out of both sides.
Report any contaminated item found in clean storage to the dental nurse or the practitioner.

workedExamples.situation: At changeover, a cleaner is asked to wipe the chair arm and the light handle, and then restock the glove boxes.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Where do the boxes go, and which gloves are used for the wiping?
workedExamples.reasoning: Restock the boxes in the clean storage area, not beside the chair. Put on fresh gloves for the wiping, because gloves worn while assisting are not used for cleaning.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a tray of used instruments sitting on a shelf in clean storage.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not handle the contaminated items with bare hands or move them further. Tell the nurse or practitioner so the items go back to the instrument area under the practice's process.

equipmentAndPpe: Fresh gloves, one pair for each changeover task
Neutral detergent wipes or solution, as the practice protocol specifies
Protective covers or wraps for hard-to-clean equipment

commonErrors.error: Reusing gloves that were worn while assisting.
commonErrors.prevention: Change gloves before any wiping task.

commonErrors.error: Storing glove boxes next to the chair.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep bulk stock on the clean side, covered.

commonErrors.error: Carrying a bag into the room.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave personal items on the clean side.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The division and the boundary of each side are set in the practice's written protocol. Follow the protocol where it is more specific than this lesson.
Splashes and aerosols are routes of exposure. Standard precautions apply whenever you clean on the contaminated side.
Australian guidance on zoning comes from the Dental Board's guidance and the NHMRC guideline.

qualityStandard: Gloves are changed before every wiping task at changeover.
No contaminated item is found in clean storage at the close of a session.
documentationEvidence: Changeover cleaning checklist with the time and room
Report of any item found out of its place
summary: The contaminated side is where fluids land, and the clean side holds stock and sterile items.
Movement runs from the clean side toward the contaminated side, and contaminated items never return to clean storage.
Fresh gloves are used for every cleaning task at changeover.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should a cleaner put a box of gloves they are restocking?
options: On the chair arm in the operatory for the patient.
Outside the contaminated side, in the clean storage area.
In the operatory, beside the patient's chair, for quick access
Next to the instrument wash basin in the dirty area.

knowledgeChecks.question: At changeover, you need to wipe the chair controls. Your gloves were worn while assisting. What do you do?
options: Keep the same gloves to reduce waste.
Put on fresh gloves for the cleaning task.
Spray the chair from the doorway and leave.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which movement pattern is correct in a dental operatory?
options: Contaminated items go back into clean drawers if they are quick to move and the drawers are then closed.
Stock moves from the clean side into the contaminated side, and contaminated items do not return to the clean side.
Items may move in either direction once the lid is closed and the surface is wiped down after each move.
Only the clinician may move items between the two sides and the nurse must sign for each move.
